advices.diagnosis: The OrderManager class aggregates four distinct responsibilities (order storage, pricing, audit logging, and notification) resulting in a high method count (NOM=25) and cyclomatic complexity (WMC=49). The LCOM4 value of 4 indicates the class is split into four weakly connected sub‑graphs, i.e., low cohesion. DCC=8 shows it already depends on many internal types, and extracting responsibilities will increase that count further. All attributes are private (DAM=1.0), which is fine, but the overall design is a classic God object.

suggestions.title: Extract each component into its own class

advices.risk_notes: Refactoring will require updating all call sites that previously used OrderManager's methods directly; missing delegations could cause runtime errors. The increased number of classes may complicate dependency injection and require adjustments in unit tests. If the system relies on the current monolithic state (e.g., serialization of OrderManager), those mechanisms must be revised.
